item.title: High-resolution binding data of TFIID and cofactors show promoter-specific differences
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77758-9

Here, the authors use ChIP-nexus to map all TFIID subunits and cofactors across the Drosophila genome at base pair resolution, revealing a general TFIID organization across promoter types with promoter-specific TBP and NC2 binding.
item.dc:title: High-resolution binding data of TFIID and cofactors show promoter-specific differences

item.title: Meta-analysis of empirical evidence on biodiversity and the risk of asthma
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77643-5

Biodiversity loss is associated with several adverse health effects. Here, the authors report the results of a meta-analysis investigating the effect of exposure to high environmental and human biodiversity on the risk of asthma.
item.dc:title: Meta-analysis of empirical evidence on biodiversity and the risk of asthma

item.title: The chromatin-organizer Satb1 modulates regulatory T cell activity within the tumor microenvironment
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78360-9

Identifying differences in Treg subtypes to disrupt the activities of tumor-promoting Tregs remains a challenge. Here, the authors report that Treg expression of SATB1 distinguishes pro-tumorigenic Tregs from Tregs that maintain immune homeostasis.
item.dc:title: The chromatin-organizer Satb1 modulates regulatory T cell activity within the tumor microenvironment

item.title: Lung environment in healthy old age shapes the phenotype and CCR2-mediated recruitment of a subset of apoptotic, high-turnover alveolar macrophages
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78156-x

Immune system changes in healthy aging are implicated in systemic inflammation known as ‘inflammaging’. Here the authors examine the phenotype and function of alveolar macrophages (AM) in mice, non-human primates and humans and identify an age-associated increase in a CD11c+CD11b+ AM population and in mice, demonstrate increased CCR2-dependent recruitment of monocyte-derived AMs and an association between Fas/FasL signaling, inflammation, and altered AM turnover in the aged lung.
item.dc:title: Lung environment in healthy old age shapes the phenotype and CCR2-mediated recruitment of a subset of apoptotic, high-turnover alveolar macrophages

item.title: Deep diffractive optical neural networks for detecting skyrmionic topologies of light and their live training
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77376-5

The article presents the first direct detector of optical skyrmionic topologies using a deep diffractive neural network, enabling seamless detection of symbols encoded in skyrmionic topology. Its simplified phase layers reduce network complexity and enable in situ training.
item.dc:title: Deep diffractive optical neural networks for detecting skyrmionic topologies of light and their live training

item.title: Integration of high-κ oxide on 2D semiconductors with carbon-dot monolayer assembly as van der Waals interfacial layer
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78053-3

The integration of high-κ dielectric materials with 2D semiconductors remains an important challenge for the industrialization of 2D electronics. Here, the authors report the application of a carbon-dot monolayer assembly to facilitate the deposition of high-κ HfO2 on monolayer graphene and MoS2, enabling the fabrication of high-performance transistors.
item.dc:title: Integration of high-κ oxide on 2D semiconductors with carbon-dot monolayer assembly as van der Waals interfacial layer

item.title: Suppression of spectral gap and flat bands on a cuprate superconductor side-surface
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78020-y

The authors use focused-ion-beam milling to expose the (110) side surface of overdoped La2xSrxCuO4, where a zero-energy topological flat band is expected. Angle-resolved photoemission experiments do not show the expected flat-band peak due to broadening of the flat band by Anderson-type disorder.
item.dc:title: Suppression of spectral gap and flat bands on a cuprate superconductor side-surface

item.title: Post-fabrication reconfiguration of hydrogels through thermodynamic asymmetry in dynamic chemistry
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 07 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78292-4

Dynamic covalent chemistry has provided powerful routes to dynamic polymer networks, yet the nature of the dynamic bond is typically defined at the outset and remains unchanged. Here, the authors introduce thermodynamic asymmetry in dynamic covalent chemistry to enable the reconfiguration of network-defining linkages after material formation, allowing for functional material evolution.
item.dc:title: Post-fabrication reconfiguration of hydrogels through thermodynamic asymmetry in dynamic chemistry
